post.description:
Support-safe cancellation: applies the SAME cancellation-policy math a
self-service guest cancel would (see refunds.quote_refund) — no custom
percentage. Use this for ordinary "please cancel my booking" tickets.
`initiated_by="host"` gives a full refund (e.g. the host cancelled and
support is processing it on the guest's behalf); it does not accept
"system" — that path is for internal automation only.

For anything that needs to deviate from policy (goodwill refund, dispute
outcome, safety incident) use POST /refund, which is full-admin only.

Chargeback / dispute lifecycle on a booking: none → open → won|lost.
Support agents can open one (they take the issuer's call); the money
consequence of a LOST dispute is the full-admin refund override above.
Opening a dispute also holds any not-yet-paid payout for the booking —
money must not go out to the host mid-dispute.

Admin-triggered refund — overrides the cancellation policy. Used when
the host is at fault / safety incident / dispute outcome.

post.description:
Verify an email with a code WITHOUT signing anyone in.

Backs the one-click link in sign-up emails: the web /verify-email page
calls this, so the click can happen on any device — no session is issued,
the user returns to the app and logs in normally. The code alone proves
inbox ownership, same trust as /password/register/verify.

Server-side logout — revokes THIS token's jti until its natural expiry.

Clients still clear their local copy; this makes the discarded token dead
on the server too (a stolen token can no longer ride out the 14-day TTL
after the user logs out). Idempotent, never fails the client's logout.

Verify a Google ID token, Facebook access token, or Apple identity
token from a mobile client and return a backend JWT. No
INTERNAL_API_SECRET needed — the provider token itself proves identity.

Creates the account and emails a code, but issues no session: the
account only becomes usable through /password/register/verify.

Rejects any existing email — verified or not, OTP/OAuth/password —
rather than attaching a password to it, since nothing here proves inbox
ownership. The one exception is another unconfirmed sign-up: it never
worked, so a fresh sign-up replaces it (otherwise anyone could squat an
address by registering it first).

Reuses the email-OTP challenge — same code, same delivery path as
email-OTP login. Always looks like success, even for an unknown email,
so the response can't be used to enumerate registered addresses.

Exchange a provider-verified identity for a backend JWT.

Trusts the caller because:
  1. The endpoint is only called from the Next.js server, never the browser.
  2. The X-Internal-Secret header must match INTERNAL_API_SECRET. Without
     that match the request is rejected as 401.
  3. The Next.js server obtained `provider_id` from the OAuth provider's
     verified id_token (OIDC) or graph API — Aangan never sees the raw
     OAuth tokens, only the resolved identity.

User resolution order:
  a. Lookup by provider_id (returning user).
  b. Lookup by email (existing phone user adding social) → link.
  c. Create new user (OAuth-only; phone stays NULL until later).

post.description:
Client-confirm — instant UI flip. In live mode the webhook is authoritative and
will arrive shortly to reconcile. If signature verification fails here we mark
the payment failed and decline the booking.

Razorpay webhook receiver.

Configured in Razorpay dashboard → Webhooks → endpoint URL `/api/payments/webhook`,
secret = RAZORPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET, subscribed to at minimum:
    payment.captured · payment.failed · payment.authorized · refund.processed

Razorpay retries non-2xx for up to 24h. We:
  1. Read the raw body (signature is over bytes — never parse first).
  2. Verify HMAC SHA-256 with the webhook secret.
  3. Look up the event_id; if already seen, ack and return.
  4. Dispatch to a per-event-type handler.
  5. Always return 200 once persisted, even if dispatch errored — we own
     retrying internally rather than letting Razorpay re-deliver, which
     would race against operator fix-ups.

Manually schedule a payout for one booking. In production a background job
runs this for every eligible booking each day.
